newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds off, premium coupons bought.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds off, premium coupons bought.

text.p: Further backup in U.S. interest rates prompted purchases of premium-coupon U.S. mortgage-backed securities on Monday, traders and analysts said.
Mortgages lost ground overall, keying off declining Treasuries to fall nearly half a point in discount coupons. But spreads narrowed modestly as Treasuries slipped further.
Some investors bought slightly premium coupons, sensing no imminent rush to refinance, traders said.
"There's been good retail buying in (Ginnie Mae) 8.0s and 8.5s," one trader said.
While discounts were off 11/32 to 13/32, premiums were off 1/32 to 9/32.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper -- the current coupon -- was off 11/32 at 100-4/32 late on Monday, yielding 115 basis points over 10-year Treasuries.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac certificates were off 9/32 at 100-1/32 and 100-05/32, respectively.
The 10-year note had fallen 14/32 to 100-28/32, yielding 6.38 percent.
